scroll_of_cure_wounds.name: scroll of cure wounds
scroll_of_cure_wounds.lore: Out of the hill country of Gilead the caravans bore a fragrant resin down to Egypt for medicine, and when the prophet Jeremiah grieved for his people he asked if there was no balm in Gilead. Apprentice healers copy a short blessing over that balm onto cheap parchment, which closes a cut and steadies the reader when it is read aloud, though it can do little more.

scroll_of_healing.name: scroll of healing
scroll_of_healing.lore: The masters of Salerno, on the coast south of Naples, kept the first school of medicine in Europe. They taught from Greek, Latin, Arabic and Hebrew books and numbered women among the teachers, and they set their best remedies in verse so that the students would remember them. One such verse is written here, and by it an honest wound is mended.

scroll_of_vigor.name: scroll of vigor
scroll_of_vigor.lore: The abbess Hildegard of Bingen, who wrote two books of medicine in the twelfth century, beheld one force at work in the rising sap and in healthy flesh alike, and named it viriditas, the greening power. This rite calls upon that power, so that wounds close over as a tree heals around a nail.

scroll_of_rejuvenation.name: scroll of rejuvenation
scroll_of_rejuvenation.lore: When Aeson, the father of Jason, had grown old and failing, Medea rode nine nights in her chariot to gather herbs. She stirred them with an olive stick until it sprouted leaves, and when she had drained the old man's blood and filled his veins with the brew, he rose up forty years younger. By the like art this rite restores a badly broken body in one reading.

scroll_of_full_restoration.name: scroll of full restoration
scroll_of_full_restoration.lore: The archangel Raphael, whose name means 'God heals', went once in disguise as a hired guide, as the Book of Tobit tells, and at the journey's end he taught Tobias to cure his father's blindness with the gall of a fish, so that the old man saw his son and wept. This is the greatest of all the healing rites, and death itself hesitates over the one who reads it.

scroll_of_local_mapping.name: scroll of local mapping
scroll_of_local_mapping.lore: Before Theseus entered the Labyrinth, Ariadne gave him a ball of thread, and he tied one end at the door and followed it out again when he had killed the Minotaur at the centre. A surveyor's rough shorthand does the work of that thread for the ground round about, and draws in the reader's mind every passage for a long way about him, near half the floor.

scroll_of_area_mapping.name: scroll of area mapping
scroll_of_area_mapping.lore: When the surveyors of Rome laid out roads and camps they carried the groma, a staff crowned with a cross and hung with a plumb line at each arm. By sighting along two of the lines they found a perfect right angle, and for this cause their towns are square still. A journeyman's scroll sights down the corridors in the same fashion, for a good distance in every direction, until the most of a floor is drawn.

scroll_of_cartography.name: scroll of cartography
scroll_of_cartography.lore: The pilots of the Middle Ages steered by portolan charts, each drawn upon a single calfskin, with every harbour named along the coast and a web of compass lines across the sea. The oldest that endures is the Carta Pisana, made about 1290. This scroll draws the passages of the dungeon as those pilots drew their coast, and carries the line round every bend, until the whole floor is charted.

scroll_of_deep_mapping.name: scroll of deep mapping
scroll_of_deep_mapping.lore: On the isle of Samos, in the sixth century before Christ, the engineer Eupalinos drove a water tunnel a full kilometre through a mountain, and his two crews dug from opposite sides until they met almost exactly in the middle. Such knowledge of rock is held within this scroll, by which the whole of a level takes shape before the reader, room after room, and every door hidden in the rock shows itself.

scroll_of_dungeon_mapping.name: scroll of dungeon mapping
scroll_of_dungeon_mapping.lore: About the year 1300 a cleric drew the whole world upon one calfskin for Hereford Cathedral, with Jerusalem at the centre, Paradise at the top, and hundreds of towns, beasts and marvels between, and there it hangs still. With as great ambition this scroll was drawn for a single floor, and it is the truer map, for every corridor, stair and hidden door appears upon it at once, and every snare laid in the floor besides.

scroll_of_identify.name: scroll of identify
scroll_of_identify.lore: The goldsmiths of Lydia would rub a coin upon a slab of black stone and judge it by the colour of the streak, and they named that slab the touchstone, for it could not be deceived. The same virtue was ground into the ink of this scroll, and as one streak tells the gold of a whole purse, so this scroll, touched to any one thing the reader chooses, gives the true name and nature of it and of every other unknown thing of its sort that he carries.

scroll_of_identify_two.name: scroll of discernment
scroll_of_identify_two.lore: Two women came before King Solomon with one living child, and each swore that it was hers. He called for a sword to divide the baby, and by this he knew the true mother, for she cried out that she would give it up. With like discernment this scroll judges every unknown thing the reader carries, and whatever lies at his feet, and names each one truly.

scroll_of_identify_three.name: scroll of appraisal
scroll_of_identify_three.lore: At the feast of King Belshazzar a hand appeared and wrote upon the plaster, and none of the wise men of Babylon could read it until Daniel read out the three words, numbered, weighed and divided, and that night the kingdom fell. An appraiser keeps this scroll among his stock, for it reads every unknown thing in the pack as plainly, and every one lying within sight besides, and names them honestly.

scroll_of_mass_identify.name: scroll of mass identify
scroll_of_mass_identify.lore: In the morning of the world, when as yet there was no other work to do, God brought every beast of the field and bird of the air before Adam to see what he would call them, and whatever he called each one, that was its name. This rite leads the same procession through the pack and across the whole floor, and every unnamed thing the reader carries, or that lies anywhere on that level, is named.

scroll_of_omnisight.name: scroll of omnisight
scroll_of_omnisight.lore: Argus Panoptes, the all-seeing, had a hundred eyes and never closed more than a few of them at once, and when Hermes slew him Hera set those eyes in the tail of the peacock. This rite opens every one, so that each hidden name in the pack and on the whole floor is read, and every carcass among the baggage gives up its lore as well.

scroll_of_sharpen.name: scroll of sharpen
scroll_of_sharpen.lore: As Odin went in disguise through the world he showed nine farmhands a whetstone that put a finer edge on their scythes than any other, and when all nine desired it he tossed it in the air, so that they cut one another down in reaching for it. A smith's first scroll has less virtue than that stone, but it will take upon any blade, and more deeply when the parchment itself has been blessed.

scroll_of_weapon_blessing.name: scroll of weapon blessing
scroll_of_weapon_blessing.lore: Before a new knight belted on his sword, a blessing from the old pontificals was read over the blade, asking that it defend churches, widows and orphans. A temple armourer copied out that prayer upon this scroll, and the weapon in hand comes away from the reading keener and truer than ever the smith left it.

scroll_of_enchant_weapon.name: scroll of enchant weapon
scroll_of_enchant_weapon.lore: Between the ninth and eleventh centuries the smiths of the Franks sold swords with a name inlaid in iron down the blade, Ulfberht, between two crosses, and so fine was their steel that forgers copied the name and misspelled it. The inscription that this scroll writes is a true one, and both the blade in hand and the bow upon the back will take it.

scroll_of_weaponsmith.name: scroll of the weaponsmith
scroll_of_weaponsmith.lore: King Nidud cut the hamstrings of Wayland the Smith and held him upon an island to forge for the crown, and there Wayland made him marvellous things, until he had taken his revenge and flew away on wings of his own making. The mail shirt of Beowulf was called Wayland's work, and so is this rite, for it betters both the blade in hand and the bow made ready, and betters each twice.

scroll_of_legendary_edge.name: scroll of the legendary edge
scroll_of_legendary_edge.lore: Odin drove the sword Gram into a tree, and none but Sigmund could draw it out. It broke in his last battle, and the smith Regin reforged the pieces for his son Sigurd, who in proving it split the anvil to its base and afterward cut a tuft of wool that drifted against it in a stream. Such is the edge that this rite gives to the reader's weapons.

scroll_of_bracing.name: scroll of bracing
scroll_of_bracing.lore: When the boy David would go out to fight, Saul dressed him in the royal bronze helmet and coat of mail, but after a few steps David said that he could not go in armour he had not proved, and he put it all off again. By the armourers' bracing-rite a piece of kit is fitted to its wearer, and it holds the better when the parchment has been blessed.

scroll_of_armor_blessing.name: scroll of armor blessing
scroll_of_armor_blessing.lore: On the eve of his knighthood a squire would bathe and clothe himself in white, and then lay his armour on the altar and keep watch over it on his knees until morning. A temple armourer wrote down the blessing that was spoken at that dawn, and when it is read over worn harness it strengthens a couple of pieces.

scroll_of_enchant_armor.name: scroll of enchant armor
scroll_of_enchant_armor.lore: Beowulf, before he sailed to face Grendel, asked one thing only of his king, that if he died his mail shirt should be sent home, because Wayland had made it. No guild scroll can promise the hand of Wayland, but this one is a fair copy of his method, and it draws several pieces of worn armour tighter and harder.

scroll_of_armorer.name: scroll of the armorer
scroll_of_armorer.lore: So well did the Missaglia family of Milan fit their plate in the fifteenth century that princes sent their measurements across the Alps rather than trust a smith at home, and upon every piece was struck the family's mark. The mark of such a master is on this rite, by which most of a harness is reinforced, and reinforced well.

scroll_of_legendary_ward.name: scroll of the legendary ward
scroll_of_legendary_ward.lore: Since no weapon could pierce the Nemean lion, Heracles strangled it, and afterward no knife would skin it until he thought to use the beast's own claws. He wore that hide for the rest of his life, and by this, the greatest of the armourers' rites, every piece that the reader wears is made very nearly as stubborn.

scroll_of_uncurse.name: scroll of uncurse
scroll_of_uncurse.lore: Certain monks who wished to be rid of their abbot, Benedict of Nursia, handed him a cup of poisoned wine, and as he made the sign of the cross over it, which was his custom before every meal, the cup shattered. An acolyte's rite copies that gesture, and by it one cursed thing that the reader wears lets go.

scroll_of_purity.name: scroll of purity
scroll_of_purity.lore: Before Sunday Mass the priest walks the nave sprinkling the people with blessed water, while the choir sings the verse of the psalm about being washed whiter than snow, and the rite is named the Asperges from its first word. The monks made this copy of it to do the same for gear, and it releases everything cursed that the reader wears.

scroll_of_cleansing.name: scroll of cleansing
scroll_of_cleansing.lore: Upon the Day of Atonement the high priest laid both hands on a live goat, confessed over it the sins of all Israel and sent it away into the wilderness, and English names it the scapegoat. An exorcist's rite loads a burden in the same manner and drives it forth, so that curses fall from worn gear and afflictions from the body.

scroll_of_purification.name: scroll of purification
scroll_of_purification.lore: The folk of Egypt buried their dead with a papyrus named the Book of Coming Forth by Day, whose most famous spell holds a list of forty-two denials, one for each judge in the hall where the heart is weighed against a feather. This liturgy pleads as thoroughly for its reader, until every cursed thing carried, whether worn or stowed, is unbound.

scroll_of_sanctification.name: scroll of sanctification
scroll_of_sanctification.lore: When Isaiah saw the Lord enthroned he cried that he was a man of unclean lips, but a seraph flew to him with a live coal, taken from the altar with tongs, and at its touch upon his mouth his guilt was gone. This rite likewise does more than cleanse, for it lifts every curse and leaves one worn piece blessed.

scroll_of_ward.name: scroll of ward
scroll_of_ward.lore: Israel was bidden by the Law to write its words upon the doorposts of the house, and to this day a small case holding a strip of parchment, the mezuzah, is fixed to the right side of a Jewish door. The watchmen made their charm after that manner, and it settles a thin guard upon the reader, which soon fades.

scroll_of_protection.name: scroll of protection
scroll_of_protection.lore: The prayer that is called Saint Patrick's Breastplate binds the one who speaks it to the strength of heaven: Christ before, behind, beneath, above, on the right hand and the left. Patrick sang it on the road to Tara, as tradition tells, and his enemies saw only deer go by. The acolytes of the temples copy it out, and its words close around the reader with Christ before and behind, on the right hand and the left, so that nothing that circles the reader finds a side unguarded.
scroll_of_protection.ward_line: Christ before and behind, on the right hand and the left: no pack that circles you finds a side unguarded

scroll_of_greater_protection.name: scroll of greater protection
scroll_of_greater_protection.lore: For two thousand years men and women have worn the ninety-first Psalm upon scraps of papyrus, in lockets, and sewn into the coats of soldiers, because it promises that no terror by night nor arrow by day will come near the one who trusts. This rite is the whole Psalm written out by a careful hand, and the guard it raises endures, so that no arrow that flies by day and no terror by night comes near the reader while the words hold.
scroll_of_greater_protection.ward_line: No arrow that flies by day and no terror by night comes near you while the words hold

scroll_of_aegis.name: scroll of aegis
scroll_of_aegis.lore: Hephaestus made the aegis for Zeus, a goatskin fringed with a hundred golden tassels and bearing the head of the Gorgon at its centre. Athena wore it into battle more often than her father did, and not even his thunderbolt could break it. The scribes of her temple wrote this rite in its likeness, so that blades find little purchase on the reader, and the Gorgon at its centre looks back at any gaze that seeks the reader.
scroll_of_aegis.ward_line: The Gorgon at the shield's heart looks back at any gaze that seeks you

scroll_of_absolute_ward.name: scroll of absolute ward
scroll_of_absolute_ward.lore: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego were cast bound into the furnace of Nebuchadnezzar, which had been heated seven times hotter than its wont, and the king looked in and saw four men walking loose in the fire. The three came out with not a hair singed and no smell of smoke upon their coats. This is the longest and strongest of the warding rites, and for as long as it lasts fire has no claim on the reader.
scroll_of_absolute_ward.ward_line: As the three in the furnace walked in the fire unburnt, fire has no claim on you

scroll_of_bewilderment.name: scroll of bewilderment
scroll_of_bewilderment.lore: In July of the year 1518 a woman named Frau Troffea fell to dancing in a street of Strasbourg and could not stop, and within a month hundreds had joined her. The council hired pipers and built a stage, but these brought no cure. A tavern conjurer's scroll passes on a mild case of that madness, so that every enemy in sight staggers for a few moments.

scroll_of_confusion.name: scroll of confusion
scroll_of_confusion.lore: Odysseus told the Cyclops that his name was Nobody. When the blinded giant screamed for help and his neighbours called through the rock to ask who was hurting him, he roared that Nobody was hurting him, so they told him to pray and went back to bed. This rite sows as great a muddle among every enemy in view.

scroll_of_madness.name: scroll of madness
scroll_of_madness.lore: Pentheus, king of Thebes, forbade the worship of Dionysus, and for this the god sent the king's own mother to dance among the women in the hills. When Pentheus crept up to spy, she took him for a mountain lion, and she had carried her trophy home before her eyes cleared. With such madness this working unmoors every creature in sight, and for a long while.

scroll_of_drowsing.name: scroll of drowsing
scroll_of_drowsing.lore: Singing as she went, Medea walked up to the sleepless dragon that guarded the Golden Fleece, dipped a sprig of fresh-cut juniper in her potion and sprinkled its eyes until the great head sank, and Jason took the Fleece from the oak. A soothing-charm was made after her manner, and it causes everything in sight to nod for a brief while.

scroll_of_sleep.name: scroll of sleep
scroll_of_sleep.lore: The house of Sleep, as Ovid tells, is a cave where the sun never enters, and it has no door, lest a hinge should creak. The river Lethe murmurs over pebbles at its foot and poppies grow at its mouth. From those poppies the ink of this scroll was pressed, and at its reading every creature in sight sinks down together.

scroll_of_deep_slumber.name: scroll of deep slumber
scroll_of_deep_slumber.lore: Seven young Christians of Ephesus hid in a cave from the emperor Decius, and he had the entrance walled up. When a farmer broke the wall they awoke and sent one of their number to buy bread, and the coins he carried were nearly two centuries old. A shadow of that long sleep is laid by this working upon all in view.

scroll_of_quickness.name: scroll of quickness
scroll_of_quickness.lore: When the Persians landed at Marathon the men of Athens sent their runner Pheidippides to ask the help of Sparta, and by the second day, as Herodotus tells, he had covered about a hundred and fifty miles of mountain road. A courier's charm lends his legs to the reader for a short stretch, and gives two strides in the time of one.

scroll_of_haste.name: scroll of haste
scroll_of_haste.lore: After the fire had fallen on Carmel, Elijah warned King Ahab to harness his chariot before the rain should stop him. Then the hand of the Lord came upon the prophet, and he tucked his cloak into his belt and ran ahead of the horses all the way to Jezreel. By this scroll the swiftness of that run is given to the reader.

scroll_of_alacrity.name: scroll of alacrity
scroll_of_alacrity.lore: Camilla, the warrior maiden who led the cavalry of the Volsci against Aeneas, was so light of foot, as Virgil sang, that she could cross a field of standing wheat and bend no ear, and skim the sea without wetting her feet. Her lightness is in this greatest of the rites of speed, which lasts far longer than any other.

scroll_of_blink.name: scroll of blink
scroll_of_blink.lore: The prophet Habakkuk was carrying stew to the reapers in Judea when an angel took him by the hair and set him down in Babylon, beside the lions' den where Daniel sat hungry, and when he had handed over the dinner he was carried back again. An apprentice's scroll moves its reader as suddenly, but gives no word of where that will be.

scroll_of_teleportation.name: scroll of teleportation
scroll_of_teleportation.lore: The ships of the Phaeacians had no need of helmsmen, for they knew every harbour and steered by thought alone. One of them bore Odysseus home in a single night, and its crew laid him asleep on the beach of Ithaca and were gone before the dawn. As sure as those ships is this working, which sets its reader down somewhere already walked.

scroll_of_recall.name: scroll of recall
scroll_of_recall.lore: The Sibyl warned Aeneas that the road down to Avernus is easy, since the door of the dark stands open night and day, but that the labour lies in climbing back. The surveyors of the deep caves took her at her word, and made this rite to fold space until the reader stands at the head of the stairs going down.

scroll_of_spark.name: scroll of spark
scroll_of_spark.lore: In the 1780s Luigi Galvani touched the leg of a dissected frog with two different metals, and when it kicked he believed that he had found the animal's own vital spark. This charm of an artificer's apprentice passes such a twitch into tired wands, and the two most spent in the pack each regain a little.

scroll_of_charging.name: scroll of charging
scroll_of_charging.lore: Alessandro Volta doubted the frogs of Galvani, and in 1800 he piled up discs of zinc and silver with card soaked in brine between them, and drew from the pile a steady current. Napoleon made him a count for it, and the unit of electrical pressure bears his name. This rite stacks those discs afresh, so that every wand carried gains a charge.

scroll_of_recharge.name: scroll of recharge
scroll_of_recharge.lore: A widow of Zarephath in a time of famine shared with Elijah her last handful of flour and her last drop of oil, and from that day her jar was never empty and her jug never ran dry until the rains came. Out of the same bounty this great working fills every wand in the pack to its brim.

scroll_of_light.name: scroll of light
scroll_of_light.read_line: Hero's lamp kindles at your shoulder and goes where you go
scroll_of_light.lore: Hero, the priestess of Sestos, set a lamp each night in the window of her tower, so that Leander might swim the Hellespont to her by its light. A candle-lighter's cantrip kindles that lamp once more at the reader's shoulder, and it goes where he goes for a long while, lighting the dark ahead of him, though it shows him to the dark as well.

scroll_of_illumination.name: scroll of illumination
scroll_of_illumination.read_line: A spark of the Pharos kindles above you and goes where you go
scroll_of_illumination.lore: The Pharos of Alexandria was raised by Sostratus of Cnidus about 280 years before Christ in three tiers of pale stone, and stood among the tallest buildings on earth, with a fire at the top that ships beheld some thirty miles out. This rite kindles a spark of that beacon above the reader, brighter than any lamp, and it goes with him through a floor and more, though like the Pharos it is seen from far off.

scroll_of_revelation.name: scroll of revelation
scroll_of_revelation.read_line: The brightest of lights kindles about you, and your eyes grow as sharp as Lynceus's
scroll_of_revelation.lore: Lynceus was the lookout of the Argonauts, for his eyes could pierce the trunk of an oak and the ground beneath it, and from a mountain top he once spied out a man who lay hidden inside a hollow tree. This greatest working of light kindles the brightest of lights about the reader and lends him the lookout's eyes, so that for a long while nothing invisible is hidden from him, and for a time he sees through stone itself.

scroll_of_enchant_ring.name: scroll of enchant ring
scroll_of_enchant_ring.lore: Eligius the goldsmith was so honest that when King Clotaire gave him gold for one throne he made two and handed back both. He became a bishop afterward, and jewellers still keep his feast. This rite is of his workmanship, and it makes each of a pair of worn trinkets a little more than it was before.

scroll_of_trinketry.name: scroll of trinketry
scroll_of_trinketry.lore: So unbroken was the luck of Polycrates of Samos that a friend warned him to throw away what he valued most. He rowed out and let his emerald signet fall into the sea, but some days later a fisherman brought him a fine fish as a gift, and the ring was inside it. With a fortune as stubborn as his, this rite improves a few of the trinkets that are worn.

scroll_of_master_trinketry.name: scroll of master trinketry
scroll_of_master_trinketry.lore: Brokkr and Sindri, the dwarf brothers, wrought for Odin the gold arm-ring Draupnir, from which eight new rings of equal weight drip every ninth night. Odin laid it on the pyre of Baldr, and Baldr sent it back to him out of the land of the dead. Under this working every ring and amulet that is worn takes a share of that plenty.

scroll_of_enchantment.name: scroll of enchantment
scroll_of_enchantment.lore: When Israel built the Tabernacle in the desert, the Lord called by name the craftsman Bezalel of Judah, whom he had filled with skill to work gold, silver and bronze, to cut stones and to carve wood. A rite for all manner of gear has need of hands like his, good at everything, and by it a few of the worn pieces are improved, of whatever kind.

scroll_of_greater_enchantment.name: scroll of greater enchantment
scroll_of_greater_enchantment.lore: Loki wagered his own head that the dwarf Brokkr could never match the treasures of the sons of Ivaldi, and then became a fly and bit the smith on the eyelid at the bellows. Yet Brokkr won the wager, though the handle of his hammer came out short. The greater rite has all the thoroughness of a dwarf, so that a good share of the reader's kit comes away well bettered.

scroll_of_grand_enchantment.name: scroll of grand enchantment
scroll_of_grand_enchantment.lore: Thetis found Hephaestus sweating at his bellows over twenty tripods on golden wheels, which would roll unaided to the feasts of the gods and home again, and he came limping to greet her upon the arms of golden maids who could think and speak. This working sends through that god's own forge whatever the reader wears.

scroll_of_stone.name: scroll of stone
scroll_of_stone.lore: Five kings of the Amorites fled from Joshua down the pass of Beth-horon, and great stones fell upon their army out of the sky, so that, as the book says, more died by the hailstones than by the sword. A stone-caller's rite makes a small likeness of that day, in which rock drops on every enemy in sight, and the sharper the reader's mind, the harder it falls.

scroll_of_earth.name: scroll of earth
scroll_of_earth.lore: When Korah and his company rose against Moses in the desert, Moses declared that if these men died a common death he had not been sent, and the ground split beneath their tents, swallowed them alive with all they owned, and closed again. This rite opens the roof where that day opened the floor, and boulders fall on all in view.

scroll_of_cataclysm.name: scroll of cataclysm
scroll_of_cataclysm.lore: Typhon of the hundred serpent heads stood taller than the mountains, and the gods fled from him as far as Egypt. But Zeus fought him across the world and at last hurled Mount Etna on top of him, and the smoke of it is his breath. In the same fashion this working drops a mountainside on everything the reader can see.

scroll_of_smiting.name: scroll of smiting
scroll_of_smiting.lore: Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron, filled their censers and offered before the Lord a fire that he had not commanded, and fire came out from his presence and consumed them where they stood, while Aaron held his peace. A white flash of like kind leaps from this short rite, and takes a few of the weakest creatures in sight.

scroll_of_annihilation.name: scroll of annihilation
scroll_of_annihilation.lore: At midnight the Destroyer went through the land of Egypt from house to house, and passed over wherever the blood of a lamb marked the doorposts, but where there was none it took the firstborn, and a great cry went up. This rite sends some likeness of that night through a room, and of all that stands in sight the lesser half is gone.

scroll_of_extinction.name: scroll of extinction
scroll_of_extinction.lore: Sennacherib of Assyria, who had taken forty-six walled towns already, pitched his camp before Jerusalem, and in one night the angel of the Lord went through it. When morning came a hundred and eighty-five thousand lay dead, and the king turned homeward. So it is with this rite, for when it ends only the very mightiest are left standing.

scroll_of_purge.name: scroll of purge
scroll_of_purge.lore: In the year 1284, as the legend goes, a piper in many-coloured clothes came to Hamelin and offered to deal with its rats, and he played until every rat in the town had followed him into the river Weser and drowned. This working plays that one tune, and the commonest kind of creature in sight leaves the floor entirely.

scroll_of_genocide.name: scroll of genocide
scroll_of_genocide.lore: There are no snakes in Ireland, nor ever were, yet the Irish give the credit to Patrick, who is said to have fasted forty days on a mountain in Mayo and then driven every serpent on the island into the sea with his staff. A harsher clearance is made by this rite, for it erases from the floor the two commonest kinds in sight.

scroll_of_exile.name: scroll of exile
scroll_of_exile.lore: Whenever Pharaoh begged, Moses prayed, and the plagues lifted as completely as they had come. The frogs died in the houses and fields, the flies departed until not one remained, and a west wind carried the locusts into the sea, so that not a single locust was left in all Egypt. Under this working every lesser kind in sight is taken away as wholly.

scroll_of_slow_time.name: scroll of slow time
scroll_of_slow_time.lore: As King Hezekiah lay dying he asked for a sign that he would recover, and when Isaiah offered him a choice he chose the harder thing, and the shadow on the stairway of Ahaz went backward ten steps. The lesser rite of a chronomancer takes back a few moments in like manner, and in them none moves but the reader.

scroll_of_time_stop.name: scroll of time stop
scroll_of_time_stop.lore: Zeno of Elea held that an arrow in flight fills at every instant a space exactly its own size, so that at every instant it is at rest, and he asked when it could ever move. Philosophers argued the matter for two thousand years, but this scroll grants him his argument, and for a time all things but the reader are at rest.

scroll_of_timeless.name: scroll of timeless
scroll_of_timeless.lore: Joshua had need of daylight to finish the battle at Gibeon, and when he spoke in the sight of all Israel the sun stood still over Gibeon and the moon over the valley of Aijalon for about a whole day, and there has been no day like it. This great working gives to its reader a long stretch of that same stillness.

scroll_of_power.name: scroll of power
scroll_of_power.lore: Milo of Croton, who won the wrestling at six Olympic Games, trained himself, so the story goes, by lifting a newborn calf onto his shoulders every day until it was a full-grown bull. All those years of his are gathered by this rite into one reading, so that the weakest of the reader's faculties is raised, and stays raised.

scroll_of_greater_power.name: scroll of greater power
scroll_of_greater_power.lore: Martianus Capella wrote in the fifth century an allegory of a wedding, where seven bridesmaids each brought one of the arts: Grammar, Logic, Rhetoric, Geometry, Arithmetic, Astronomy and Music. Schools taught those seven for the next thousand years, and this rite gives the whole of that education at a sitting, so that the reader's weakest faculty is raised for good.

scroll_of_great_power.name: scroll of great power
scroll_of_great_power.lore: Porphyry of Tyre, writing about the year 270 a short introduction to the logic of Aristotle, set all that exists upon one branching tree, from substance down to Socrates, and students copied it out for a thousand years. The whole of that tree is drawn upon this scroll, and by it the two weakest of the reader's faculties are permanently raised.

dead_sea_scroll.name: Dead Sea Scroll
dead_sea_scroll.unidentified_name: a brittle parchment sealed in a clay jar
dead_sea_scroll.lore: For two thousand years this scroll lay sealed in a clay jar in a cave near the sea, and its power comes from that long survival rather than from anything written upon it. Read it, and the shape of the whole dungeon is preserved in your mind in the same way, with the walls, the corridors and the stairs, though not the shadows that walk between them.

scroll_of_the_labyrinth.lore: Sealed with the mark of the Cretan Labyrinth. A reward scroll from Dad -- show him this code!

scroll_of_the_pasture.lore: Sealed with a brand shaped like a cow bell. A reward scroll from Dad -- show him this code! Moo.

scroll_of_nine_hells.name: Scroll of the Nine Hells
scroll_of_nine_hells.unidentified_name: a scroll bound with blood-red wax
scroll_of_nine_hells.lore: Dante counted nine circles in his Inferno, which narrow like a funnel to the frozen lake at the bottom with a different ruin set in each, and for every circle the demon Asmodeus pressed a seal upon this vellum in wax the colour of old blood. When the nine are broken together every lesser creature in sight is unmade, though the mightiest stand untouched.
scroll_of_nine_hells.design_notes: Asmodeus L92 boss reward. Wired via monster.treasure.boss_scroll_id.

scroll_of_chromatic_doom.name: Scroll of Chromatic Doom
scroll_of_chromatic_doom.unidentified_name: a scroll shifting through five colors
scroll_of_chromatic_doom.lore: Tiamat was the salt sea and the mother of the first gods, as the creation poem of Babylon tells, and when they killed her husband she bore eleven monsters and went to war. Marduk caught her in a net, split her like a dried fish, and from one half of her made the sky. The lore of dragons gave her in after days five heads and five colours, and this scroll speaks for all five at once, so that nothing lesser in sight outlives it.
scroll_of_chromatic_doom.design_notes: Tiamat L85 boss reward. Wired via monster.treasure.boss_scroll_id.

autographed_stray_kids_photo.name: Autographed Stray Kids Photo
autographed_stray_kids_photo.lore: This glossy photo of Stray Kids, alive and grinning, is scribbled all over with eight autographs in black marker, with a few gold stars stuck on for luck, and it is still warm. Read the names aloud and they might come back for one more song, a short show for you with no fighting on either side, and anything near them will stop to watch, though the photo will be gone when you have called them.

scroll_of_the_lemuria.name: scroll of the Lemuria
scroll_of_the_lemuria.lore: Each May the Romans drove the hungry dead out of their houses, and at midnight the father of the house walked barefoot, threw nine black beans over his shoulder without a backward look and said, with these I redeem me and mine. Then the shades took up the beans and left the living in peace, for so long as the living did not turn and strike them.
scroll_of_the_lemuria.read_line: You throw nine black beans over your shoulder without looking back. The restless dead will not strike you up close until you strike one

scroll_of_the_hamelin_piper.name: scroll of the Hamelin Piper
scroll_of_the_hamelin_piper.lore: A piper in a coat of many colours came to Hamelin in 1284, as the legend tells, and offered to rid it of rats for a price. He played in the streets until every rat in town came out to follow him, and so he led them into the river Weser to drown. His tune is written down upon this scroll, and any vermin that hear it must go where it leads.
scroll_of_the_hamelin_piper.read_line: You play the tune written on the scroll, and every vermin in sight must go where it leads.
scroll_of_the_hamelin_piper.none_line: You play the Piper's tune, and no rat or crawling thing in sight hears it.

scroll_of_daniel.name: scroll of Daniel
scroll_of_daniel.lore: King Darius was tricked into casting his friend Daniel to the lions because he prayed to his God, and at dawn the king came running to the den. From within it Daniel answered that an angel had shut the lions' mouths, and that they had not touched him all night. Those words, read aloud, close the jaws and sheathe the claws of the great beasts, until you lift your hand against them.
scroll_of_daniel.read_line: You read how the angel shut the lions' mouths. Great beasts will not bite or claw you until you strike one

scroll_of_the_psylli.name: scroll of the Psylli
scroll_of_the_psylli.lore: The Psylli of Libya, as Pliny wrote, bore in their bodies a poison deadly to snakes, and they tested their babies by laying them among serpents. When Cato's army crossed the desert, as Lucan sang, the Psylli went at its side and sucked the venom out of bitten soldiers. Their old charm is written here, and while it holds a serpent's bite is no more than a bite.
scroll_of_the_psylli.read_line: You speak the Psylli's old charm. A serpent's bite cannot poison you and no serpent can hold you

scroll_of_the_heart_sutra.name: scroll of the Heart Sutra
scroll_of_the_heart_sutra.lore: Hoichi was a blind lute-player who sang the Tale of the Heike so well that the ghosts of the drowned Heike called him night after night to their graves. To save him his priest wrote the Heart Sutra over every inch of his body, that the ghost-samurai might not see him, but in his haste he forgot the ears. Read over yourself, the sutra hides you from every ghost, yet it has one weak place as the priest's had, for if you strike one ghost all of them will find you.
scroll_of_the_heart_sutra.read_line: You read the sutra over every inch of your skin. The ghosts cannot see you, but strike one and they will all find you

scroll_of_saint_martha.name: scroll of Saint Martha's Hymn
scroll_of_saint_martha.lore: A dragon called the Tarasque dwelt in the Rhone and burned the farms of Tarascon, until Martha went out to it alone, as the Golden Legend tells. She sprinkled it with holy water and sang to it, and when it had grown tame as a lamb she led it into the town upon her girdle. Her hymn still takes the heat out of a dragon's breath and the weight out of its blows.
scroll_of_saint_martha.read_line: You sing Saint Martha's hymn. Dragons hurt you half as much, breath and bite alike

scroll_of_the_udug_hul.name: scroll of the Udug Hul
scroll_of_the_udug_hul.lore: The exorcists of Babylon treasured a long series of clay tablets, the Udug Hul, against the evil spirits that crept in at doors and under beds. The priest would name each demon, bind it by the great gods and order it out into the desert, and those old words, when they are copied onto vellum, still drive fiends back from the one who reads them.
scroll_of_the_udug_hul.read_line: You name the evil spirits by the great gods and order them out into the desert. Demons cannot strike you up close, and their curses and terrors do not take hold, until you strike one
